quotes.text: Enable or disable offline mode on your readers.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: When a network connection is restored, the SDK automatically forwards any stored payments to Stripe.
Click **Edit** or **Override** next to the **Offline mode** icon.
The offline mode setting updates on the reader within 10 minutes.
You can specify offline mode when creating or updating a

findings: The November 7, 2026 base capture states that the feature enables or disables offline mode on readers and indexes Dashboard and API variants. It does not contain the linked variant bodies.

The May 1, 2026 guide describes storing payments on a POS device while connectivity is intermittent, limited or absent. On restored connectivity the Terminal SDK forwards stored payments to Stripe. Separately, a merchant can update or override a location configuration in Dashboard and must apply the change after updating the toggle. The reader setting updates within ten minutes. The separate API branch demonstrates creating or updating Configuration with offline.enabled set true.

The existing summary appropriately routes offline payment behavior to separate guides and reflects the old Configuration object. Its same-hierarchy line is contextual, and its ten minutes wording should preserve May’s within-ten-minutes bound. The old feature guide's Dashboard examples operate via location edits of local or inherited settings.
substantive_changes: No product-behavior delta is established. The November capture keeps the description and replaces embedded Dashboard/API prose with links to two use-case variants.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Preserve the May local-storage and forwarding trigger with the POS device and SDK actors, two Dashboard location paths, apply step, reader-setting propagation bound, Configuration create/update and the offline.enabled example. Keep payment forwarding separate from successful processing.
Preserve the existing routes to operational payment behavior and card collection. Keep May as the source of setting mechanics and use November for variant navigation.
conflicts: The May location selection line says change the passcode, while the actual adjacent row and toggle say Offline mode. Avoid treating a passcode change as part of the documented offline-mode workflow.

The summary's 10 minutes phrasing drops the source's within condition. The separate November Configuration create/update captures show optional offline transaction settings at create lines 44–45 and update lines 58–59, but do not supply the November functional variant’s nested details or timing.
unresolved_questions: The November index cannot resolve current Dashboard controls, configuration precedence, propagation, compatible device implementation, storage or forwarding details. The omission of the functional bodies is not evidence those behaviors changed.

findings: Add the dated navigation capture and reciprocal stripe-terminal-hardware-orders link. Keep the May detail route and existing offline payment/collector links, and scope the separate Configuration object authority.
conflicts: Describe the May reader propagation as within ten minutes and preserve Update then Apply changes. Treat the old passcode wording as inconsistent with the Offline mode steps.
source_assessments.reason: The November variant links are useful new navigation. The functional requirements remain grounded in the dated prior guide.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/fleet/offline-mode, source-stripe-terminal-offline-mode-config should present the November 7, 2026 capture as an offline-mode introduction and links for Dashboard and API. See new raw lines 5-14. The index itself gives no implementation steps, prerequisites or transaction state transitions. The May 1, 2026 full capture describes the merchant's POS device storing payments locally under intermittent, limited or absent connectivity, then the Terminal SDK automatically forwarding the stored payments to Stripe when connectivity returns. Forwarding is the described transition. See old raw lines 8-10. To change the setting, the merchant edits an existing relevant configuration or first creates one. From Dashboard location details or Manage locations, they select the Offline mode control, toggle, update and apply changes. The reader setting updates within ten minutes. The API branch uses Configuration create or update, with offline.enabled true in the examples. See old raw lines 16-37 and old raw lines 39-74. The current summary keeps the May toggle and separate offline payments/collection routes, but its ten-minute shorthand should retain the upper bound and its account/location hierarchy should route to the wider Configuration authority.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/fleet/offline-mode, use the November 7, 2026 capture as a navigation raw reference in source-stripe-terminal-offline-mode-config. The feature sentence remains; the old expanded Dashboard and API sections are replaced by explicit variant links. See new raw lines 5-14, old raw lines 4-16 and old raw lines 39-45. There is no demonstrated functional change. Preserve May 1, 2026 evidence for local POS storage, automatic SDK forwarding after network recovery, location edits and apply step, configuration update within ten minutes and API create/update. See old raw lines 8-10, old raw lines 18-37 and old raw lines 43-74. The old location selection wording says passcode, but adjacent instructions explicitly select Offline mode (old raw lines 18-25). Preserve the reciprocal stripe-terminal-hardware-orders route, link the Terminal Configurations hierarchy source, and keep source-stripe-terminal-offline-payments and source-stripe-terminal-offline-collect-card-payments as distinct integration routes. The separate November Configuration create/update references list optional offline settings. The base offline-mode capture does not confirm the old operational constraints for November, and omission does not prove removal.
